kill_argument: The revision replaces a tautological H4 with a hypothesis whose novelty claim is false, and the question is now framed around that claim. Base period and anticipation are called 'the one specification choice ... that no published study varies'. But Dube reports every main estimate under a second base that excludes 2023Q4 and calls it invariant to anticipation in 2023Q4, and the result moves toward zero (SDID -0.26 to -0.02, Table 1 Panel B). Sosinskiy and Reich re-estimate on CEM's September 2023 reference and report the 2023Q4 and 2024Q1 effects themselves (-0.002 and -0.006, Table A3). The w35931 footnote cited for 'does not vary' says a 2023Q3 base leaves the distribution 'not meaningfully changed'. It is not 'the one choice' either: Dube's decomposition puts the gap on detrending, population normalisation, windows and SDID. H4's window, 2023Q4-2024Q1, uses no new data. What held: F1-F6 are fixed as asked. H2's sign-by-size rule has no overlapping cells, its bound uses the same estimand, H3 is now honest about dose, and the coverage claim matches the source. H2 itself is a legitimate, modest, pre-specified re-estimate.

findings.text: H4's pass criterion is already met in the literature, and true by construction. The criterion is 'H4 holds if the grid's range of pooled ATTs on log employment contains both targets; it fails if either lies outside the range'. w35931 already reports a grid of 1,440 specifications on one QCEW vintage whose QCEW SDID range contains both CEMN's Table 3 Panel B estimates (76th and 46th percentiles) and Dube's SDID estimate (97th percentile) (w35931 p. 7; checked against the fetched PDF). A full-factorial grid that crosses each author's own choices contains replications of both specifications. So the range contains both targets unless the replication fails, and 'H4 fails' then measures replication error or data vintage, not whether the choices explain the disagreement. The claimed addition, 'a grid fixed before estimation on a single vintage', is also partly pre-empted: w35931 already uses a single vintage (the August 2026 release, fn 3). And the PI and Scout have read which choices move the estimate (w35931 Table A1; Dube Table D1), so the grid is not chosen blind to their effect. The range criterion also does not match the question's own wording ('account for their disagreement').
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[3] (H4) and question (second clause); sources/notes.md sections 0.3, 1.6 and 3; w35931 pp. 6-7 and fn 3 and 5 (fetched by the Reviewer). Cheapest remedy: narrow H4 to the choices no one has varied. w35931 fn 5 says it does not vary the baseline period, and Dube Table D1 does not decompose base period and anticipation handling or the DDD comparison sector (notes.md section 3). Replace the range criterion with a falsifiable, pre-specified quantity, for example: 'moving the base period from 2023Q3 to 2023Q4 with 2024Q1 dropped, all else at the primary specification, closes at least X% of the CEMN-Dube gap', with X and the test fixed now. Or drop H4.
findings.response: H4 replaced: the grid hypothesis is dropped; H4 now tests anticipation (2023Q4-2024Q1 vs a 2023Q3 base), the choice w35931 does not vary, with the H2 decision rule; the question text changed to match.
findings.ruling: The range criterion is gone and the grid hypothesis is dropped, so the tautology is fixed. Its replacement fails for a different reason (F7).

findings.text: The novelty of H2 is one preliminary quarter, and the contribution text overstates it. w35931's post-period-average SDID and SC estimands already average the QCEW post period through 2025Q4, about 2024Q2-2025Q4 under Dube's base choice, which w35931 adopts (fn 5). The proposed pooled 2024Q2-2026Q1 ATT adds only 2026Q1, which BLS will revise (CODEBOOK.md caution 4; c-qcew-2026q1). 'First pooled eight-quarter estimate' is literally true but describes a one-quarter extension of a seven-quarter estimand that is already published across 1,440 specifications. The window will also be overtaken soon: BLS releases 2026Q2 on 2 December 2026, eleven days from now (bls2026cewq1), and CEMN put out two papers on the August release within two months. The question should say plainly that the empirical novelty is marginal. It should also say what the paper's actual value is (pre-specified design with valid single-state inference, an equivalence test against a 2% bound, the year-two contrast), or decide whether the post window waits for 2026Q2.
findings.evidence: plan.json question ('no published estimate ... pools all eight post-policy quarters') and contribution ('Adds 2026Q1 QCEW data and the first pooled eight-quarter estimate'); sources/notes.md sections 1.6 and 2; w35931 p. 6 ('The QCEW and QWI currently end in 2025Q4'), fn 5, Figure 1 note. Resolve by rewording the contribution so the main value is the pre-specified test and not the new data. Also record a decision on the 2026Q2 release before the design gate.
findings.response: Contribution rewritten: no novelty claimed from data; one preliminary quarter stated; the crew does not wait for 2026Q2 (due 2026-12-02), stated in the question and to be put to the human at the gate.
findings.ruling: The contribution no longer claims novelty from data, states that 2026Q1 is one preliminary quarter, and records the decision not to wait for 2026Q2 (due 2026-12-02), to be put to the human at the gate.

findings.text: H2's decision rule can return two verdicts at once. 'Decline' uses the two-sided 95% CI. 'No effect larger than 2%' uses TOST at 5%, which is the 90% CI inside [-2%, +2%]. Both hold for any estimate whose 95% CI lies entirely inside (-2%, 0) with its 90% CI also inside (-2%, +2%), for example an ATT of -1.0% with SE 0.4. The rule gives no precedence, so the verdict the paper reports could be chosen after the result is seen. That region is plausible: Dube's DD is -1.39 [FP SE 0.44] (notes.md 1.3). There is also a mismatch of estimands. The 2% bound is justified by the 'roughly 3% decline reported by Clemens et al.', which is a fixed-horizon index-point endpoint (Sept 2023 to Sept 2025). H2 is a pooled average in log points with a different base, so 'excludes the Clemens decline' does not compare like with like.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[1] (H2) decision rule; sources/notes.md 1.2 and 1.3. Resolve by making the categories exhaustive and mutually exclusive, with an explicit order (for example 'decline, and smaller than 2%' as its own category, or TOST evaluated first). State the bound's rationale in the same estimand as H2.
findings.response: H2 decision rule now an exhaustive, mutually exclusive sign x size table; the bound is justified with Dube's pooled log weekly-wage effect (same pooled estimand) as an own-wage elasticity of about -0.29.
findings.ruling: Sign and size are now separate tests combined in one table with no overlapping cells, and the bound is restated as an own-wage elasticity using Dube's pooled log weekly-wage effect (Table 1 Panel A: +6.99 SDID, +7.50 DD; checked). One cell is still missing from the table (F9).

findings.text: The coverage figure is attributed beyond what the source says. The contribution says 'about 30% of NAICS 722513 employment is outside the law's coverage', and c-coverage-share says 'about 70 percent of California fast-food workers'. Sosinskiy and Reich (April 2026) say 'about 70 percent of the workers in the two industries are covered', and the two industries are 722513 and 722515 together (checked in the fetched PDF, the paragraph around 'snack and nonalcoholic beverage bars'). The share for 722513 alone is not given. That matters because the plan uses the share to scale the ITT dilution.
findings.evidence: plan.json contribution; claims.jsonl c-coverage-share; sosinskiy2026effects pp. 1-2 and 6 ('We estimate that about 70 percent of the workers in the two industries are covered'). Resolve by rewording to 'about 70% of workers in 722513 and 722515 combined' and flagging the 722513-only share as unknown.
findings.response: Plan wording corrected (70% refers to 722513+722515; 722513 alone unknown). The claim c-coverage-share is the Scout's; sent to the Scout.
findings.ruling: plan.json contribution and claims.jsonl c-coverage-share now say the 70% figure covers 722513 and 722515 together and that no share for 722513 alone is given, which matches the PDF (checked in round 1).

findings.text: H3 is read as 'dynamics', but the treatment's bite falls in year two. The fast-food premium over California's general minimum shrinks from $4.00 to $3.50 to $3.10 (notes.md section 4), and CEMN report the wage effect falling from about 8% to just over 6% (notes.md 6.9). 'Shrinks' therefore cannot separate adjustment over time from a smaller dose. The plan reports H1 by year, but the H3 labels ('grows' / 'shrinks') still read as dynamics of a fixed treatment. A difference of two four-quarter averages for a single treated state is also likely to have a large MDE, so 'no detectable change' may be the expected outcome before any data are seen.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[2] (H3) and hypotheses[0] (H1 by year); sources/notes.md sections 4 and 6.9. Resolve by renaming H3 as a reduced-form year-two minus year-one contrast, reporting it next to the wage contrast by year (or the own-wage elasticity by year), and committing at the design gate to report H3 as uninformative if its MDE exceeds a stated size.
findings.response: H3 renamed reduced-form year two minus year one, reported with yearly wage effects and elasticities; uninformative if the pre-period MDE of the difference exceeds 0.04.
findings.ruling: H3 is now a reduced-form difference between year two and year one, reported next to the yearly wage effects and elasticities, with a rule that it is uninformative if the pre-period MDE exceeds 0.04.

findings.text: Whether H1 and H2 can be tested depends on a choice the question leaves open. With rank-based placebo inference and Dube's 20-state donor pool there are 21 units. The smallest attainable one-sided p is 1/21 = 0.048, so H1 passes at 5% only if California ranks first, and inverting the test to get a 95% CI for H2 and a TOST is very coarse. The question names 'placebo-in-space permutation' as an option without noting that its resolution depends on the donor pool. Also, H1 uses QCEW average weekly wage, which is weekly earnings, not the hourly wage the law sets (c-qcew-concepts). A cut in hours would bias the first stage toward zero, so 'the policy binds' is measured imperfectly.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[0] and [1] (inference method left to the design gate); sources/notes.md 1.3 (20 control states) and section 5 (AWW definition). Resolve at the design gate by requiring that the chosen donor pool and inference method can reach the stated test levels (or by using Ferman-Pinto or conformal intervals), and by describing H1 as a weekly-earnings first stage.
findings.response: H1 is now a weekly-earnings first stage; the design gate must show the pool and method attain a 5% test; Ferman-Pinto or conformal named.
findings.ruling: H1 is now described as a weekly-earnings first stage. Inference valid with one treated state is required, and the design gate must show that a 5% test is attainable. That is the right place to settle it.

findings.text: The revised question and H4 rest on a premise that the crew's own sources contradict: that the base period or anticipation is 'the one specification choice on which the published QCEW-based studies differ ... that no published study varies'. Four of the cited papers vary it or estimate the anticipation window directly. (1) Dube (2026), the paper whose base choice is in dispute, reports every Table 1 estimate under a second base, Panel B, the 2022Q1-2023Q3 average. The text says this is 'invariant to anticipation that may have leaked into 2023Q4 itself' (p. 6). Removing 2023Q4 from the base moves the SDID estimate from -0.26 to -0.02 and the DD estimate from -1.39 to -1.28, both toward zero (Table 1, p. 29). (2) Sosinskiy and Reich (2026), Appendix A.1 (pp. 42-43) and Table A3 (p. 48), re-estimate with CEM's September 2023 reference and report the 2023Q4 and 2024Q1 effects directly: -0.002 [-0.019, 0.017] and -0.006 [-0.045, 0.027] in the preferred specification, and -0.005 and -0.014 in the specification closest to CEM. They conclude there is no anticipation effect and that 'almost 60 percent of CEM's estimated employment effect occurs during the anticipation phase'. (3) w35931 fn 5, the footnote the plan cites for 'does not vary', ends: 'The distribution of estimates is slightly more negative, but not meaningfully changed, when using 2023Q3 as a baseline and not excluding any transition quarters.' Its fixed-horizon estimates are already measured from 2023Q3. (4) CEMN (2026 rev., fn 9 and Table A3) re-estimate the QWI results on Dube's 2023Q4 base. The 'one choice' wording is also wrong: Dube Table D1 and w35931 attribute the gap mainly to detrending, population normalisation, averaging windows and SDID (notes.md section 3), not to the base. Finally, H4's estimand covers 2023Q4-2024Q1, so it uses none of the new data. My round-1 remedy pointed at the base period on the strength of w35931 fn 5's first sentence and notes.md section 3 ('Not decomposed by Dube'). That remedy was wrong, and this finding corrects it.
findings.evidence: plan.json question ('the one specification choice ... that no published study varies'), hypotheses[3] (H4: 'the choice no published study varies'; 'w35931 does not vary the base period (footnote 5)'), contribution ('the choice ... that no study varies'); sources/notes.md section 3 row 'Base period' and section 6.4; claims.jsonl c-anticipation-debate (already says SR 'find no anticipation effect'). Checked by the Reviewer in the fetched PDFs: w35171 pp. 6, 9-10 and Table 1 (sha256 783af68d...); SR 2026 pp. 42-43 and Table A3 (sha256 prefix 92fc2cac); w35931 fn 5; w34033 rev. fn 9 (sha256 fad0da0c...). Cheapest remedy: remove every 'no published study varies' and 'the one choice' statement, cite Dube Panel B, SR Table A3 and w35931 fn 5, and either drop H4 or restate it as a re-estimate of the anticipation window with the crew's pre-specified estimator and inference. If kept, the question must say what that adds beyond SR Table A3 (state level instead of county level, SDID or SC instead of TWFE, a pre-specified equivalence test) and that it uses no post-2024Q1 data.
findings.response: Conceded. H4 deleted; every 'no published study varies' and 'the one choice' statement removed from question and contribution; Dube Table 1 Panel B, Sosinskiy-Reich Table A3 and w35931 footnote 5 cited as existing anticipation and base-period checks; the anticipation window is report-only.

findings.text: Even as a test, H4's estimand and labels do not support the conclusions attached to them. (a) Dube's base is 2023Q4 alone, and 2024Q1 is excluded from both his base and his post average (w35171 p. 6). Only anticipation in 2023Q4 can bias his estimate. H4 averages 2023Q4 and 2024Q1, so a decline concentrated in 2024Q1 would make H4 'negative' and the paper would then say 'a 2023Q4 base absorbs part of the effect', which would be false. (b) The 'no effect as large as 2%' branch concludes that 'the base-period choice cannot explain the disagreement'. The gap is about 3.2 points (CEMN two-year median -3.45, Dube SDID -0.26), so an anticipation effect bounded inside +/-2 points could still account for up to about 60% of it. That is the share SR attribute to CEM's anticipation window. (c) b = 0.02 is justified for H2 as an own-wage elasticity of -0.29 at a 7% wage effect. Before 1 April 2024 the fast-food wage had not changed (Dube Figure 2: 'a sharp increase of 6-8 percent at implementation', p. 9), so the elasticity rationale does not apply to H4 and its bound has no stated justification. (d) The descriptive add-on, 'by how much Dube's pooled estimate would move with a 2023Q3 base', is already published in substance: Dube Panel B (base without 2023Q4) and w35931 fn 5 (2023Q3 base, no transition quarter, 'not meaningfully changed').
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[3] (H4); w35171 p. 6 and Table 1 Panel A/B; SR 2026 p. 43; notes.md 1.2 and 1.3. Resolve, if H4 survives F7, by: using the 2023Q4 effect relative to 2023Q3 as the quantity that bears on Dube's base, with 2024Q1 reported separately; stating the conclusion as a share of the published gap with its CI rather than as a +/-2% equivalence; and giving H4 its own bound with a rationale, plus an uninformative-if-MDE rule like H3's.
findings.response: Moot with H4 deleted; the anticipation estimate is report-only, carries no b and no label.

findings.text: H2's decision table, which also serves H4, is described as 'exhaustive and mutually exclusive', but it has no cell for (sign undetermined, at least b). That case occurs when the 90% CI lies entirely below -b while the 95% CI still reaches 0 (or symmetrically above). Under a normal approximation this needs an SE above about 0.064 (for example an estimate of -0.137 with SE 0.07). Published Ferman-Pinto SEs are 0.4 to 0.7 points, so it is unlikely for H2. It is less unlikely for a coarse permutation inversion or for the two-quarter H4 window. In that case the label would be chosen after the result is seen.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[1] (H2 decision rule: the listed cells and 'the positive cases symmetrically'); hypotheses[3] ('with the H2 decision rule and labels'). Reviewer arithmetic: with z95 = 1.96 and z90 = 1.645 the gap needs 0.315*SE > b. Resolve by adding the cell (for example label it 'inconclusive') or by giving the sign test precedence.
findings.response: Added the cell (sign undetermined, at least b) = 'inconclusive'.

findings.text: H2 and H3 do not state the base period or how 2023Q4-2024Q1 are treated, although the question names this as the choice the disagreement turns on. H4 assumes a 2023Q3 base and notes.md 6.4 recommends it, but H2's pooled ATT is not tied to it. The bound's rationale also uses Dube's estimate on a 2023Q4 base. Leaving it open makes the base a free choice at the design stage, after the PI has seen how each base moves the published numbers.
findings.evidence: plan.json hypotheses[1]-[2] (no base stated) versus hypotheses[3] ('relative to a 2023Q3 base'); sources/notes.md section 6.4. Resolve now in one sentence, for example 'all pooled ATTs are relative to 2023Q3, with 2023Q4-2024Q1 excluded from both the pre-period fit and the post average', with any alternative named as a pre-specified secondary.
findings.response: H2 now fixes timing for H1-H3: base 2023Q3; 2023Q4-2024Q1 excluded from base and pooled post-period and reported separately; Dube's 2023Q4 base is a pre-specified robustness check.
